# race-assets — arcade racing game asset set

Procedurally generated, standards-based assets for a small arcade racer (stylised-realistic, bright daytime).
**Everything in this folder is generated by the scripts in `/asset-src` and is rebuilt from scratch with**

```sh
make assets        # or: npm run assets
```

`manifest.json` (validated against `manifest.schema.json`) is the machine-readable description of every
file, node name, metric and transform. This README is the human summary. Exact numbers (triangle counts,
positions, hashes) live in the manifest. `reports/` holds the last validator and verification output.

## Conventions

| | |
|---|---|
| Models | glTF 2.0 binary (`.glb`), PBR metallic-roughness |
| Axes / units | right-handed, **+Y up**, **1 unit = 1 m**, forward = **−Z** (cars, spawns, checkpoints, prototypes) |
| Textures | PNG, power-of-two, ≤ 2048². Albedo = sRGB; normal + ORM = linear |
| Normal maps | tangent space, glTF/OpenGL convention (+Y up); meshes ship `TANGENT` attributes |
| ORM | R = ambient occlusion, G = roughness, B = metallic (plug the same image into occlusion + metallicRoughness) |
| Colliders | in the default scene but hidden in three ways: `KHR_node_visibility {visible:false}`, `extras.collider = true`, and material `collider_invisible` (alpha 0, `alphaMode: MASK`). They never render even if the engine ignores the extension. Feed them to physics and skip them for rendering. |
| Empties | nodes without a mesh, `extras.empty = true` |
| Track textures | `track.glb` / `scenery.glb` reference `../textures/*.png` as external files (shared, not duplicated). `car.glb` embeds its textures. |

## Contents

```
cars/car.glb                 sporty coupé, ~9.2k triangles incl. wheels
track/track.glb              circuit + baked scenery + collision + empties
track/scenery.glb            scenery prototypes (proto_*) for GPU instancing
track/racing_line.json       [{x,y,z,speed_kmh}], 442 points, closed loop
track/minimap_1024.png       top-down outline, transparent background
textures/                    ground (asphalt, kerb, grass, gravel: albedo/normal/ORM 1024²),
                             barrier, facade, billboard atlas, car liveries (4 colours)
sky/sky_equirect_2048x1024.png   background sky (equirectangular)
sky/sky_env_256x128.png          blurred low-res version for environment lighting
audio/*.wav|*.ogg            44.1 kHz mono: engine idle/mid/high loops, collisions, tyre screech loop,
                             nitro, countdown beeps, finish fanfare
ui/icons/*.svg|*_64|128|256.png   nitro, pause, camera, reset, steer_left, steer_right, brake
ui/fonts/RussoOne-Regular.ttf     + RussoOne-OFL.txt (SIL Open Font License 1.1)
previews/*.png               renders of the exported files (Blender, headless)
manifest.json, manifest.schema.json, reports/
```

## Car (`cars/car.glb`)

Root node `car`. Origin is at ground level at the centre of the wheelbase; the car faces −Z and its right side is +X.

| node | |
|---|---|
| `body` | paint (variants), glass, trim, chrome, headlights (emissive) |
| `wheel_FL` `wheel_FR` `wheel_RL` `wheel_RR` | origin = rotation centre, identity rotation, spin axis local **+X**. Rolling forward = rotate about +X by `-distance / radius`. Steer = rotate about +Y. Left wheels use a mirrored mesh. |
| `brake_lights` | own material `car_brake_light`: set `emissiveFactor` from `emissive_off` → `emissive_on` (strength ×4) when braking |
| `exhaust_L` `exhaust_R` | empties at the tail-pipe tips, local +Z = exhaust flow (backwards) |
| `collider_body` | convex hull, 172 triangles, hidden |

Metrics (also in `manifest.car.metrics`): wheel radius 0.34 m, wheel width 0.255 m, track width 1.66 m,
wheelbase 2.70 m, suggested mass 1420 kg, centre of mass (0, 0.46, −0.08) m relative to the origin.

**Colour variants**: red (player, default), blue, yellow, black. They use `KHR_materials_variants` on the body
paint primitive. Engines without that extension can swap the `baseColorTexture` of material `car_paint_red` to
`textures/car_body_<colour>_albedo.png`.

## Track (`track/track.glb`)

A 2.21 km counter-clockwise circuit with a 14 m wide road. It has a ~560 m start/finish straight, a fast left
sweeper (R ≈ 120 m), a 180° left hairpin (R ≈ 20 m), a four-corner S-section, and a hill over the back straight
(+10 m crest, −3 m dip at the sweeper). Kerbs line every corner, gravel traps sit on the outside of the fast
corners, and 1 m concrete barriers close the circuit on both sides.

* **Visual**: `road` (asphalt + paint), `kerbs`, `barriers`, `terrain` (grass + gravel),
  `scenery_trees|grandstand|buildings|billboards|signs|gantry|cones`.
  18 primitives / 11 materials in total, which is the static draw-call count.
* **Collision** (hidden): `col_road` (road + kerbs, friction ≈ 1.0), `col_barriers` (closed 4 m walls on both
  sides), `col_terrain` (run-off between road edge and barrier, 3 cm below the road, friction ≈ 0.55).
* **Spawns** `spawn_1`…`spawn_4`: 2-wide staggered grid behind the line, pole on the left. Each node is a car
  origin with local −Z = race direction.
* **Checkpoints** `cp_00`…`cp_15`: evenly spaced in race order, with `cp_00` = start/finish line. The
  trigger-box size `[across, up, along]` and its local centre are in the manifest and in node `extras`.
* **Racing line**: minimum-curvature line inside the road (1.6 m margin), with a speed profile for
  ≈ 1.4 g lateral (13.5 m/s²), accel ≈ 2–9 m/s² and braking 15 m/s². `y` lies on the road surface.
* **Minimap**: `u_px = x·k + offset_px[0]`, `v_px = z·k + offset_px[1]` (k = `pixels_per_metre`, origin at the
  top-left, north = −Z = up). The same transform is given as the 2×3 matrix `world_to_map_matrix`.

### Scenery

All scenery is baked into the `scenery_*` nodes of `track.glb`, merged by material. For GPU instancing instead,
skip those nodes and instantiate the `proto_*` nodes of `track/scenery.glb` with `manifest.scenery.instances`
(world-space translation / rotation quaternion / scale, plus an optional colour tint). Prototypes: 2 tree types,
grandstand, pit building, office, control tower, 5 billboards (invented brands), chevron and distance signs,
start gantry and cones. Scenery has no colliders because everything stands behind the barriers; the cones on
the run-off are decorative.

## Environment

* Sky mapping: `u = 0.5 + atan2(d.z, d.x)/2π`, `v = 0.5 − asin(d.y)/π` (v = 0 at the top). This is identical to
  three.js `equirectUv` and to Blender's default environment mapping after glTF import.
* Sun: `manifest.environment.sun.direction` is the unit vector **towards** the sun (WSW, 50° elevation).
  `light_direction` is its negation, and the colour is linear RGB. Ambient and fog suggestions are also there.

## Audio

WAV (PCM 16-bit, 44.1 kHz, mono) plus Ogg Vorbis for every sound. The engine loops (base RPM 900 / 4000 / 7500)
and the tyre screech loop are 2.0 s long and mathematically periodic: every partial completes whole cycles and
all noise is circular. They loop sample-exactly. Pitch each engine layer by `rpm / base_rpm` and crossfade
neighbouring layers. `countdown` = three 880 Hz beeps at 0/1/2 s plus a long 1760 Hz beep at 3 s. The
individual beeps are also provided. Ogg encoders can add a few samples of padding, so use the WAVs when you
need perfect loops.

## UI

Seven flat white-on-transparent icons: SVG (24×24 view box) plus PNG at 64/128/256 px, rendered from the same
shape description. Font: Russo One (SIL OFL 1.1, licence text alongside).

## Rebuild & verification

Requirements: Python ≥ 3.10 with `numpy scipy Pillow soundfile` (`asset-src/requirements.txt`),
Blender ≥ 4.2 (headless, previews only), and Node ≥ 18 (`npm install` pulls the Khronos `gltf-validator` and `ajv`).

`make assets` runs, in order: textures → sky → audio → UI → car → track/scenery/racing line/minimap →
manifest → Blender previews → manifest (with preview hashes) → `validate` → `verify`. The build fails if:

* any .glb has a glTF-validator error, or
* the manifest fails its schema, or
* any of the gameplay or budget checks fail: the racing line is closed and lies on `col_road`, checkpoints are
  in order, spawns (including all four wheel contact points) are on the road, and the triangle and draw-call
  budgets are met.

The report is printed and saved in `reports/verify_report.txt`.
